# Finite Chebfun convolution source package

Base: 6788a09c. Candidate: ../candidate_v9. Apply candidate.patch as a patch, not a whole-class-file transplant: newer main has independent AND/OR/root orientation changes.

## Source correction

The public convolution adapter now supports native options, pairwise columns, scalar column broadcasting, row orientation, Quasimatrix operands, and empty propagation. The new JAX kernel implements the pinned Legendre convolution recurrence and native cost comparison between repeated convolution patches and quadrature. This matters for original width ratios 1e-3 and 1e-6; the former implementation would create extremely many patches. Bndfun uses the shared kernel. The `old` comparator is an independent adaptive Gauss7/Kronrod15 integral, not an alias for the new recurrence. Its cubic endpoint transform, initial panels, refinement and effective relative tolerance follow licensed R2025b integral source; the native effective relative tolerance floor is 100*eps even when caller requests 1e-15.

Original delta identity clause 9 exposed a separate concrete addition bug: overlap can move a breakpoint, but addition recomputed stored point values using the original operands. The narrow correction returns the already aligned operands from `_binary_op` only when requested by `__add__`, and uses them in its existing point-value calculation. Default `_binary_op` callers are unchanged. Four exact stored-value controls cover scalar/array and row/column orientation, plus existing PLUS regression controls.

The removed host NumPy convolution helpers have no surviving callers. The name `_easy_conv` is reused locally in the new module; all three surviving references resolve to that new local definition. AST_REVIEW.json and REMOVED_HELPER_SEARCH.txt bind the complete private source/test scan. All 331 other Chebfun methods/functions, all 67 existing Quasimatrix methods, and all 9 other Bndfun methods are AST-identical to the base.

## Scientific qualification

The permanent test file ports all 21 pinned native convolution clauses literally, preserving operation order, norms, source tolerances, fixed 80-point ATAP construction, retained clause-8 tolerance for later clauses, case-insensitive `Old`, and the source no-error predicate for clause 21. Existing source tests were not weakened. Evidence records individual original IDs; scientific gate counts are separate from repeated clauses and supplemental controls.

Baseline had two passes and three API/numerical failures among five bounded cases: options were unsupported and array convolution failed. The prohibitively expensive width-ratio baseline was not run. Development failures are preserved: incorrect tweak_domain tuple unpacking, stored-value delta identity failure before aligned addition, missing empty count adapter, and a pytest duplicate-basename collection error before scientific execution. Corrected successors are separate guarded directories.

## Native delta-prime limitation

The fresh pinned native capture ../../cvd1 is terminal, uncensored, input-stable, and has no owned survivors. Both `conv(diff(dirac(x)), step)` and the reversed order return zero smooth functions with no delta or warning. Their internal domains differ. In contrast `diff(step)` contains two half-strength delta contributions at zero, totaling one. This follows native per-FUN convolution: it differentiates a Bndfun, not the full discontinuous Chebfun. The package preserves this limitation rather than adding mathematically expected global jump deltas. A supplemental regression binds the observed output. The MAT file retains infinite pointValues that JSON represents as null.

## Scope and limits

- This qualifies the Python translations of all 21 source clauses; no fresh native run of the full 21-clause file is claimed.
- Native delta capture runtime evidence is retrospective provider observation, not prospective whole-runtime closure.
- No general coefficient-length, interior-piece-count, bitwise FFT/BLAS, or timing-ratio parity claim is made.
- The independent integral is a private finite-real, scalar-valued path. It is not a public contour/infinite integration implementation. Singfun routes to this path but singular convolution beyond these gates is not newly qualified.
- Host adaptive construction and shape decisions are not claimed JIT-compatible; numerical kernels are JAX-only.
- Native operand swapping omits options upstream in one early branch; this source behavior is retained.
- Custom nondefault constructor/session technology preferences are not separately qualified here.
- The native RNG request for future cumsum arrived after cvd1 was frozen/running. No RNG additions or extra native run were made.

Chebfun source pin: 7574c77680d7e82b79626300bf255498271a72df. Licensed quadrature source: MATLAB R2025b, distinct from the Chebfun pin. CPU4-7, pinned Python3.12.13/JAX0.11.0/x64, owned 180-second/3-GiB Python gates; native discriminator 300-second/3-GiB with short temporary paths. All limits and failures are retained in the manifest.
